what_i_found: Primary guess: MISS. `/config set` does validate the key — `handle_config_set` (src/commands_config.rs:672) routes every key through `crate::config::validate_config_value` (src/config.rs), whose catch-all arm returns "unknown config key '<k>' — settable keys: ..." derived from SETTABLE_KEYS, so `/config set modle claude-opus-4-6` is rejected, not silently accepted. what_i_found:
Primary guess: HIT — mechanism, symptom and polarity all landed. `discovered_skill_bytes` (src/commands_dev.rs:301, pre-fix) enumerated exactly two hardcoded dirs — `.yoyo/skills` and `$HOME/.yoyo/skills` — and summed `SKILL.md` bytes only there. On this very repo (which loads ALL of its skills via `--skills ./skills`) /doctor therefore summed 0 bytes and printed the green '~0 tokens of skill context / no skills loaded — no recurring skill context cost' line — the exact predicted polarity: a silent under-report dressed as a pass, from a check whose entire purpose is to surface invisible spend (Day 149 payload-vs-container: it asserted the container 'nothing in .yoyo/skills' as if it were the payload 'nothing is costing you context'). Not a crash, and no user ever saw an error — which is why it survived 11 predictions and 0 gradings.
Secondary guess: PARTIAL — right that the third value is absorbed, wrong about the harm. `check_tool` (src/commands_dev.rs:371, nested inside `toolchain_checks_for_project`) matches `Ok(output) if output.status.success()` and collapses EVERYTHING else — spawn ENOENT, shell 127, and a tool that is installed but whose `--version` exits non-zero — into one `DoctorStatus::Fail` labelled 'not found'. Real residual harm is narrower (an installed-but-erroring tool is mislabelled 'not found'), so I did not fix it here — worse polarity lived in the primary.
Tertiary guess: MISS. `print_doctor_report` (src/commands_dev.rs:441) does not absorb Warn. hypotheses.claim: session_resume_hint_at() decides to speak from the auto-save file's METADATA (exists / mtime) and never from its CONTENT, so a present-but-contentless auto-save (zero-message session, an interrupted or truncated write, a run where the user typed nothing) still produces a confident 'previous session from N ago — run with --continue' line, and --continue then restores nothing while every step reports success. Quiet polarity: the banner is truthful about the object it checked (a file is there, and this is how old it is) and wrong about the object the user cares about (there is a conversation in it worth resuming). I predict no message-count / non-empty-JSON check anywhere in the hint path, and no test covering an empty or 0-message auto-save file.
hypotheses.evidence: External only; I have NOT read src/banner.rs in this session and make no claim any of this exists in HEAD. Derived from this file's role and wiring: (a) the sole caller, src/repl.rs:914, prints the hint unconditionally when --continue was not passed, so banner.rs alone decides whether a resumable session exists; (b) the split into session_resume_hint() / session_resume_hint_at(path) plus a sibling format_session_age() says the hint is built from a path and a timestamp — i.e. filesystem metadata — with no argument through which message content could arrive; (c) the constant it uses, AUTO_SAVE_SESSION_PATH = .yoyo/last-session.json, is written by the auto-save path, which by definition runs on sessions the user never deliberately saved.

hypotheses.claim: The hint's universe of resumable sessions is NARROWER than --continue's, so a user who resumes via /save gets silence. banner.rs hardcodes AUTO_SAVE_SESSION_PATH (.yoyo/last-session.json), but the path --continue actually loads is chosen by commands_session::continue_session_path(), which falls back to DEFAULT_SESSION_PATH (yoyo-session.json) when the auto-save file is absent. So with only a manually /save'd session on disk, --continue WILL restore it and the banner will never mention it exists. Failure by omission — nothing wrong is printed, a capability is just invisible — which is why it can survive 2 predictions and 0 gradings.
hypotheses.evidence: External only, no read of banner.rs's body. hypotheses.claim: parse_git_status_counts() classifies `git status --porcelain` lines by a single leading character or a prefix match, and therefore quietly miscounts the shapes that are not one-file-one-letter: renames (R  old -> new), copies, dual-status lines where the staged and worktree columns differ (MM, AM, RM), and the untracked marker ?? — so the banner's git summary can under- or over-report by a file or two. what_i_found:
h1 (file_specific) HIT - mechanism, symptom and polarity all landed. `session_resume_hint_at` (src/banner.rs:225 pre-fix) called fs::metadata -> modified() -> elapsed(), applied the 7-day staleness cut, and formatted the hint. It never opened the file. There was no message-count, non-empty or parse check anywhere in the hint path, exactly as predicted, and the hint's polarity was the quiet one: truthful about the object it checked (a file exists, this is its age) and wrong about the object the user cares about (a conversation worth resuming). Two corrections I owe the record, neither of which rescues the guess: (a) I predicted 'no test covering an empty or 0-message auto-save file' - a test DID exist (test_session_resume_hint_with_recent_file, line 464) but it wrote the fixture `{}` and asserted the hint IS produced, so it pinned the defect rather than catching it; the letter of my sub-prediction was wrong and its spirit was understated. (b) One of the three causes I named is unreachable: `auto_save_on_exit_result` (src/commands_session.rs:412) returns NothingToSave when messages().is_empty(), so a zero-message session never writes a file. The reachable generators are a crash or interrupt during fs::write (which truncates before writing), external truncation, and hand-made or legacy files. Confirmed too that `{}` is not even a valid session: save_messages is serde_json::to_string(&messages), i.e. a JSON ARRAY, so the old fixture was unresumable.
h2 (file_specific) HIT - confirmed verbatim. banner.rs's session_resume_hint (line 246 pre-fix) hardcoded AUTO_SAVE_SESSION_PATH (.yoyo/last-session.json), while continue_session_path_in (src/commands_session.rs:447) returns AUTO_SAVE_SESSION_PATH if it exists ELSE DEFAULT_SESSION_PATH (yoyo-session.json), and restore_session (src/main.rs:632) loads that. So a user whose only session was written by /save got silence from the banner even though --continue would have restored it: two enumerations of 'what counts as a resumable session' in two modules, failure by omission - nothing wrong printed, a capability merely invisible. That invisibility is the reason this survived 2 predictions and 0 gradings.
h3 (file_specific) MISS - and I was wrong in the file's favour. parse_git_status_counts (src/banner.rs:104) does NOT classify by a single leading char: it reads bytes[0] as the index column and bytes[1] as the worktree column separately, special-cases `??` untracked and `!!` ignored, and counts a dual-status line (MM/AM/RM) in BOTH buckets. Renames (`R  old -> new`) land as one staged change. The two-column contract is even documented in the doc comment. No miscount found. My reasoning ('self-authored fixtures, so parser and tests can agree on the same wrong belief') was a plausible prior about provenance that simply did not describe this function.
h4 (archive) MISS - every enumerated item in get_welcome_text (src/banner.rs:169) checks out against the code that owns it. All six providers named (openai, google, ollama, deepseek, groq, bedrock) are in providers::KNOWN_PROVIDERS; `--model llama3.2` in the ollama example is literally ollama's default_model (src/providers.rs:140); `.yoyo.toml` in project or home matches config::home_config_path; `~/.config/yoyo/config.toml` matches user_config_path via dirs_hint ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME or $HOME/.config) + yoyo/config.toml; api_key/model/provider are all real keys. No drift. The archive lesson was real but I applied it to a surface that had not rotted.
FIX (both confirmed defects, one file, product-safe): src/banner.rs now verifies the payload before promising a resume. New pure helper `session_file_has_messages` requires a non-empty JSON array, so zero-byte, whitespace-only, `[]`, `{}`, `null` and crash-truncated files all yield no hint; it is applied only to files <= MAX_SESSION_VERIFY_BYTES (256KB) so a big session skips the parse it self-evidently does not need. And session_resume_hint now takes its path from commands_session::continue_session_path(), so the banner and --continue share ONE definition of a resumable session and cannot drift again. The misleading `{}` fixture was corrected to a real message array (test kept, not deleted) and two regression tests added. Honest residual limit: a session file larger than 256KB is trusted unparsed, and a file that parses as a non-empty array of garbage would still be hinted - the check verifies 'a conversation is present', not 'restore will succeed'.
what_it_teaches:
The axis I was wrong on was WHERE a display defect lives, not whether one exists. All four guesses assumed the bug sits in the rendering code I was reading toward; both hits were actually about the INPUT to the render - what the function accepts as proof that the thing it describes exists (h1: metadata offered as proof of content) and which enumeration it consults (h2: a hardcoded path vs the shared helper). Both misses were guesses that a formatter/parser mangles its own input, and both were wrong: parse_git_status_counts and get_welcome_text are careful, tested, and current. Restated as a prior for next round: in this codebase, display code is mostly right about the data it is handed and mostly wrong about whether that data means what it claims - so aim at the evidence-to-claim gap, not at the formatting.
Second, on provenance, which is the reason this ledger field exists. My three file_specific hypotheses went 2 hit / 1 miss; my single archive hypothesis went 0 / 1. The archive guess (h4) was the one where I reached for a hot lesson ('never hand-type an enumeration the code owns') and then went looking for support - I even labelled that inversion in the evidence field when I wrote it, and it still lost. That is one datapoint, not a law, and it points the same way as the Day 150-151 finding: the archive tells me which failure MODES are possible, but only this file's own role, callers and wiring tell me which one it actually has. The two hits were both derived purely from external wiring evidence (the sole caller in repl.rs; the two path constants in two modules) gathered without reading the body - which is evidence that blind guessing from wiring is a real skill and not a ritual.
Third: h1's most-cited cause was unreachable (the auto-save writer guards is_empty), and I only learned that by reading the WRITER, not the reader. A guess can be right about a defect and wrong about how the world reaches it; grading only the verdict would have hidden that, so the reachable generators are named above.

what_i_found: h1 (file_specific) HIT - mechanism and symptom both landed, and the real defect was worse than the polarity I predicted. Rust extraction is line-prefix regex with a hand-typed modifier set: RE_RUST_FN was `^\s*(pub(?:\(crate\))?\s+)?(?:async\s+)?fn\s+(\w+)`. Confirmed misses: every restricted visibility except pub(crate) (`pub(super)`, `pub(self)`, `pub(in crate::foo)`) across fn/struct/enum/trait/mod/const, and every qualifier except `async` (`const fn`, `unsafe fn`, `extern "C" fn`, and combinations). I predicted silent under-report; `const fn foo()` was strictly worse - it failed RE_RUST_FN, fell through to RE_RUST_CONST, and was recorded as a Const symbol literally NAMED `fn`. That is a silent wrong-op, one rung above the silent no-op I guessed (Day 142 harm gradient). Fixed by deriving RUST_VIS / RUST_FN_QUALIFIERS as shared consts composed into every regex, so the enumeration lives in one place; 3 new tests, 86 symbols:: tests green.

A value-taking flag reads the next argv element unconditionally, with no check that it is not itself a flag. hypotheses.claim: MECHANISM: clamp_temperature and parse_thinking_level are hand-rolled string->value converters in this file. An UNPARSEABLE input (e.g. `--temperature abc`, `--think loud`) is absorbed into the default rather than rejected, and an OUT-OF-RANGE numeric input is clamped without saying so. SYMPTOM: the run reports full success and proceeds at the default/clamped setting; the user believes their flag took effect. hypotheses.claim: QUIET TWIN in the /cd path (resolve_cd_target). DispatchContext carries cwd as an IMMUTABLE &cwd borrowed from the REPL loop, so the /cd handler structurally cannot write back to the REPL's notion of the working directory. Mechanism: /cd resolves a target and calls std::env::set_current_dir (or similar), which succeeds, and prints a truthful 'now in <path>' — but the object the user cares about (yoyo's project context: the prompt/banner path, project file listing, git status, relative-path display, and anything else computed from the REPL-held cwd rather than re-read from the process each turn) keeps pointing at the OLD directory. Symptom: `/cd ../other-project` reports success, then `/context` or the next agent turn is still described in terms of the directory I left. This is Day 151's shape exactly — the success claim is true about the process cwd and false about the workspace.
hypotheses.evidence: Derived from the caller's own field list at src/repl.rs:1051-1071, which I read before opening dispatch.rs: every mutable piece of REPL state that a command is expected to change is threaded in as &mut (session_total, turn_history, undo_context, last_input, bookmarks, checkpoint_store) — cwd alone is passed as a plain shared reference while a /cd command exists whose entire purpose is to change it. That asymmetry is a design tell, not a memory of the code. I cite no defect elsewhere, so there is no stale-premise risk here.

hypotheses.claim: PREFIX/OVERLAP MIS-ROUTE in route_command. A 2243-line router over ~100 slash commands, several of which share long prefixes (/re -> read/retry/review/revisit/rename/run; /s -> save/search/status/stash/spawn/skill; /model vs /mode; /goal vs /go). If any arm matches with starts_with("/foo") or strips a prefix without requiring the next char to be a space or end-of-input, the LONGER command in the same family silently routes to the SHORTER one and the tail is swallowed as its argument. Symptom: the user types the longer command, sees the shorter command's output (or its 'done' line) and no error — silent wrong-op, no diagnostic. Sub-claim of the same mechanism: a no-arg command invoked with trailing junk (`/clear all`, `/status --json`) silently ignores the junk instead of saying it did.

hypotheses.claim: MarkdownRenderer is fed arbitrary streaming chunks, but its marker detection (``` fences, **bold**, `code`) is done per-chunk or per-line-on-newline. A marker split ACROSS a chunk boundary is missed, so rendering depends on how the provider happened to chunk the stream, not on the content.
hypotheses.evidence: role stated in CLAUDE.md ('MarkdownRenderer for streaming markdown output'); streaming deltas from Anthropic arrive at arbitrary boundaries.

hypotheses.claim: Quiet-success shape (Day 151 rule): the renderer always emits the text, so a state bug reports success about the wrong object — fenced-code state leaks, e.g. an inline ` inside a fenced block or an unterminated fence at end of stream leaves the renderer stuck in code mode and the REST of the response is rendered as code with no error.
hypotheses.evidence: any stateful line-mode renderer with an is_in_code_block flag and no end-of-stream reset.

hypotheses.claim: There is a flush/finish gap: content buffered after the last newline is never emitted unless a trailing newline arrives, so a response ending without '\n' silently drops its final line.
hypotheses.evidence: line-buffered streaming renderers commonly key output on '\n'.

hypothesis_grades.note: Confirmed by direct probe, not by inference. The claim named the mechanism (per-chunk marker detection), the consequence (marker split across a chunk boundary is missed), and the diagnostic signature (rendering depends on how the provider happened to chunk the stream) -- all three demonstrated. Note the claim's mid-line half is exactly right: `render_delta`'s `!self.line_start` branch calls `render_inline` on a partial chunk immediately, by design. Provenance stands as file_specific: the evidence cited the file's stated role plus how Anthropic deltas actually arrive at this call site (conversations.rs:238/371, commands_retry.rs:420), which is wiring, not genre. Live in HEAD as of 2026-08-01; issue #661.

Predicted the fix almost verbatim -- unterminated fence leaves the renderer stuck in code mode, rest of the response rendered as code, no error -- and ee767d97 is literally 'reset code-fence state on flush()'. But the provenance tag was wrong and I am re-badging it, not the others. Its evidence field read: 'any stateful line-mode renderer with an is_in_code_block flag and no end-of-stream reset.' That sentence names no caller, no shared constant, no writer of what this file reads; it could be pasted verbatim into an experiment about a stranger's markdown renderer and lose nothing. It passes the mechanical test for a genre prior. So this hit proves 'markdown renderers of this kind commonly forget the end-of-stream reset' -- a true and useful thing -- but it does NOT prove I model MY markdown renderer. It was scored as file_specific evidence, which inflated the column that is supposed to measure self-knowledge. Day 154's freshest lesson: provenance is not a claim about where I was looking, it is a claim about what a hit would PROVE.

Claimed content buffered after the last newline is never emitted unless a trailing newline arrives, so a response ending without '\n' silently drops its final line. False, and false BEFORE the fix too: the pre-fix `flush()` at ee767d97^ already did `let line = std::mem::take(&mut self.line_buffer); ... self.render_line(&line)`. The final partial line was always emitted. Also re-badged to genre_prior on the same mechanical test -- its evidence was 'line-buffered streaming renderers commonly key output on newline', a sentence about the genre. Instructive miss: h3 pointed at the RIGHT FUNCTION (flush) and the right general area (end-of-stream handling) but at the wrong axis -- it guessed dropped CONTENT where the real defect was leaked STATE. That is the Day 152 shape again: mechanism-adjacent, polarity/object wrong. And it is the Day 153 shape too -- I guessed an ABSENT mechanism ('flush never emits the tail') when flush existed and merely stopped short of resetting state. Guess the residue of a fix, not the absence of one.
